verses.greek: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν; οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν;
verses.literal: From where come disputes and from where quarrels among you? Surely from there out of the passions of you those warring in the members of you?
verses.dgt: From where come wars and from where fights among you? Is it not from here—from your pleasures that wage war in your members?

verses.greek: ἐπιθυμεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε· φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε, καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν· μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε. οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς·
verses.literal: You desire and not have you kill and covet and not are able to obtain You quarrel and wrangle Not you have because the not to ask you
verses.dgt: You desire and do not have, so you murder and envy and are not able to obtain. You fight and wage war. You do not have because you do not ask.

verses.greek: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε, διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε, ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε.
verses.literal: You ask and not receive because wrongly you ask that in the pleasures of you you may spend it.
verses.dgt: You ask and do not receive because you ask badly, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

verses.greek: μοιχαλίδες, οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν; ὃς ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου, ἐχθρὸς τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσταται.
verses.literal: Adulteresses! Surely you know that the friendship with the world hostility the with God is? Whoever maybe therefore shall choose a friend to be of the world an enemy the of God is appointed.
verses.dgt: Adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes themselves an enemy of God.

verses.greek: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν;
verses.literal: Or think you that in vain the Scripture speaks? With envy yearns the Spirit that he settled in us
verses.dgt: Or do you think Scripture speaks in vain? “The spirit that he caused to dwell in us longs with envy.”

verses.greek: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν· διὸ λέγει· Ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν.
verses.literal: Greater however He gives grace Therefore it says: the God the proud opposes to the humble however gives grace.
verses.dgt: But he gives greater grace. Therefore it says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”

verses.greek: ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ θεῷ· ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ, καὶ φεύξεται ἀφʼ ὑμῶν·
verses.literal: do be subjected therefore the to God. do resist however the devil and he will flee from you
verses.dgt: Therefore submit to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

verses.greek: ἐγγίσατε τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν. καθαρίσατε χεῖρας, ἁμαρτωλοί, καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας, δίψυχοι.
verses.literal: do draw near the to God and He will draw near to you. do cleanse your hands you sinners and do purify hearts you double-minded.
verses.dgt: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, double-minded ones.

verses.greek: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε· ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν·
verses.literal: do be grieved and do mourn and do weep The laughter of you to mourning should be turned and the joy to gloom.
verses.dgt: Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into gloom.

verses.greek: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον κυρίου, καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς.
verses.literal: do be humbled in the presence of Lord and He will exalt you.
verses.dgt: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

verses.greek: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων, ἀδελφοί· ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον· εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις, οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής.
verses.literal: Not do speak against one another brothers The one speaking against his brother or judging the brother of him speaks against the Law and judges the Law If however the Law you judge not you are a doer of the Law but a judge.
verses.dgt: Do not speak against one another, brothers and sisters. The one who speaks against a brother or sister or judges them speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

verses.greek: εἷς ἐστιν νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής, ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι· σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ, ὁ κρίνων τὸν πλησίον;
verses.literal: One there is Lawgiver and Judge who is being able to save and to destroy You yourself however who are you who are judging the neighbour?
verses.dgt: There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the one able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

verses.greek: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες· Σήμερον ἢ αὔριον πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ κερδήσομεν·
verses.literal: do come now you who are saying Today or tomorrow we will go into such the city and will spend there a year and will trade and will make a profit
verses.dgt: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go into such-and-such a city and spend a year there and trade and make a profit,”

verses.greek: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε τὸ τῆς αὔριον ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν· ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστε ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη·
verses.literal: you who not you know what is on the next day is What is the life of you! A vapor just you are the for a little while appearing then also vanishing
verses.dgt: you who do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist appearing for a little while and then disappearing.

verses.greek: ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς· Ἐὰν ὁ κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο.
verses.literal: Instead ought the to say you If the Lord shall wish both we will live and we will do this or that.
verses.dgt: Instead you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”

verses.greek: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν· πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν.
verses.literal: Now however you boast in the arrogance of you All boasting such evil is.
verses.dgt: But now you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.

verses.greek: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι, ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
verses.literal: To him knowing therefore good to do and not doing it sin to him it is.
verses.dgt: Therefore, for the one who knows to do good and does not do it, it is sin.
